items.stem: Which is a feature of RISC processors?
options: Many complex instructions of variable length
Few registers
A small set of simple instructions, most taking one clock cycle
Instructions that operate directly on memory in many modes
items.answer: A small set of simple instructions, most taking one clock cycle
items.markingKey: RISC: fixed-length instructions, many registers, load/store architecture, easy pipelining.

items.stem: Explain why RISC processors have more general-purpose registers than CISC processors.
items.answer: RISC uses a load/store architecture: only load and store instructions access memory, so operands are kept in registers; more registers reduce slow memory accesses.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Explain how interrupts are handled in a pipelined processor.
items.answer: Instructions in the pipeline may be allowed to complete or are flushed; register contents are saved; the ISR is loaded into the pipeline; after the ISR the pipeline restarts from the saved PC.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per point, max 3 [3]

items.stem: A processor has a 3-stage pipeline; each stage takes 5 ns. Calculate the time to execute 8 instructions without pipelining and with pipelining (no hazards).
items.answer: 120 ns; 50 ns

items.stem: A processor has a 5-stage pipeline; each stage takes 1 ns. Calculate the time to execute 50 instructions without pipelining and with pipelining (no hazards).
items.answer: 250 ns; 54 ns

items.stem: A processor has a 4-stage pipeline; each stage takes 5 ns. Calculate the time to execute 6 instructions without pipelining and with pipelining (no hazards). Then calculate the speed-up.
items.answer: 120 ns; 45 ns; speed-up 2.67

items.stem: Hana works for a company in Seoul that designs processors for smartphones. (a) Explain why RISC processors are often used in smartphones. (b) Explain why a CISC program may need fewer instructions than a RISC program for the same task.
items.answer: (a) Simpler circuits use less power and generate less heat; good performance per watt. (b) Each CISC instruction can do more work (e.g. memory operands, complex operations).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Arjun works for a company in Mumbai that designs processors for smartphones. (a) Compare RISC and CISC in terms of instruction set and clock cycles per instruction. (b) Explain why RISC processors are often used in smartphones.
items.answer: (a) RISC: few simple fixed-length instructions, ~1 cycle each; CISC: many complex variable-length instructions, several cycles. (b) Simpler circuits use less power and generate less heat; good performance per watt.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each comparison, max 3 [3] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Which is a feature of CISC processors?
options: Only fixed-length instructions
Many complex instructions, some taking several clock cycles
No microcode
Instructions all complete in one cycle
items.answer: Many complex instructions, some taking several clock cycles
items.markingKey: CISC: variable-length instructions, many addressing modes, fewer instructions per program.

items.stem: What is pipelining?
options: Executing one instruction at a time from start to finish
Storing data in a cache
Running two programs on two cores
Overlapping the stages of several instructions so a new one starts before the previous one finishes
items.answer: Overlapping the stages of several instructions so a new one starts before the previous one finishes
items.markingKey: e.g. fetch, decode, execute, memory access, write back stages run in parallel on different instructions.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Interrupts must be handled carefully in a pipelined processor. Reason (R): RISC instructions are of variable length. Which option is correct?

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is true but R is false
items.markingKey: A is true; R is false: "RISC instructions are of variable length." is incorrect.

items.stem: Elena is explaining pipelining to colleagues at MetroBus in Nairobi. Explain the role of registers in a RISC processor.
items.answer: Many general-purpose registers hold operands so that most instructions work on registers, not memory, which is faster.

items.stem: Which describes SISD?
options: Many processors execute the same instruction on different data at the same time
Several processors execute different instructions on the same data
One processor executes a single stream of instructions on a single stream of data
Several processors execute different instructions on different data independently
items.answer: One processor executes a single stream of instructions on a single stream of data
items.markingKey: SISD: one processor executes a single stream of instructions on a single stream of data; e.g. an early single-core personal computer.

items.answer: The task must be split into parts that can run at the same time, and the results combined; sequential code runs on one processor only.

items.stem: What is a virtual machine?

A computer with no hardware
A program that removes viruses

items.answer: Several OSs on one computer; legacy software can be run; testing in isolation without risk to the host; easy back-up/cloning of whole systems; better use of server hardware.

items.answer: 200 ns; 60 ns

items.stem: Nadia works for a company in Lisbon that designs processors for smartphones. (a) Explain why RISC processors are often used in smartphones. (b) Explain why a CISC program may need fewer instructions than a RISC program for the same task.
items.answer: (a) Simpler circuits use less power and generate less heat; good performance per watt. (b) Each CISC instruction can do more work (e.g. memory operands, complex operations).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Ravi is comparing a RISC processor with a CISC processor for a laptop developed in Cairo. (a) Explain why RISC processors are often used in smartphones. (b) Explain how pipelining improves performance.
items.answer: (a) Simpler circuits use less power and generate less heat; good performance per watt. (b) Different stages of several instructions run at once, so one instruction completes per cycle once the pipeline is full.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) What is a massively parallel computer? (b) Which describes MIMD?
items.answer: (a) A computer with a very large number of processors working together on one task, linked by a network (b) Several processors execute different instructions on different data independently
items.markingKey: (a) e.g. supercomputers with thousands of nodes. (b) MIMD: several processors execute different instructions on different data independently; e.g. a modern multi-core processor running several programs.

items.stem: Ana is comparing computer architectures for Horizon Travel. Explain why not all programs benefit from extra cores.
items.answer: Sequential code cannot be split; overheads of communication/synchronisation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Nova Telecom in Auckland uses a computer with a multi-core processor and a GPU. Explain why the multi-core processor is described as MIMD.
items.answer: Each core can execute a different instruction stream on different data at the same time.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Which classification best describes fault-tolerant systems such as flight control, where results are compared?
options: MISD
MIMD
SIMD
SISD
items.answer: MISD
items.markingKey: MISD: several processors execute different instructions on the same data.

items.stem: A task takes 240 s on one processor. 25% of the task must run sequentially and the rest can be shared equally between 4 processors. Calculate the time taken on 4 processors and the speed-up.
items.answer: 105 s; speed-up 2.29
items.markingKey: sequential part 60 s (1); parallel part 180 ÷ 4 = 45 s (1); total 105 s, speed-up 240 ÷ 105 = 2.29 (1) [3]

items.stem: A weather forecasting centre in Kathmandu uses a massively parallel computer. (a) Explain why a massively parallel computer is suitable for this task. (b) Explain why adding more processors gives diminishing returns.
items.answer: (a) The task can be split into many independent parts (grid cells/frames) processed simultaneously, reducing time. (b) Sequential parts cannot be parallelised and communication overhead increases.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) What is the guest operating system? (b) Which is an example of a process virtual machine?
items.answer: (a) The operating system running inside the virtual machine (b) The Java Virtual Machine running bytecode
items.markingKey: (a) The host OS runs on the real hardware. (b) Process VMs run a single program (e.g. JVM); system VMs run a full OS.

items.stem: Assertion (A): A virtual machine can run an operating system that is different from the host. Reason (R): The guest system is isolated from the host and can be reset. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A and R are both true statements, but R does not explain A.

items.stem: FreshFarm Foods runs several virtual servers on one physical server in Singapore. (a) Explain why a fault in one virtual machine does not affect the others. (b) Explain why the software may run more slowly in the virtual machine.
items.answer: (a) Each VM is isolated with its own guest OS and virtual hardware. (b) Instructions and hardware access go through the emulation layer, adding overhead.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: SkyLink Airways uses a virtual machine for testing several operating systems on one computer. Which type of virtual machine is this?
options: Physical machine
Network virtual machine
Hardware emulator chip
System virtual machine
items.answer: System virtual machine
items.markingKey: System VMs run a whole guest OS; process VMs (e.g. JVM) run a single program.

items.stem: BlueWave Supermarkets in Santiago has a server with 256 GiB of RAM and 16 processor cores. The hypervisor needs 2 GiB. Each virtual machine needs 6 GiB of RAM and 2 cores. Calculate the maximum number of virtual machines that can run at once and state the limiting resource.
items.answer: 8 virtual machines; limited by processor cores
items.markingKey: memory: (256 − 2) ÷ 6 = 42 (1); cores: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 (1); 8, limited by processor cores (1) [3]

items.stem: Starlight Cinemas in Dhaka is reviewing its data centre. Discuss, with reasons, the use of virtual machines by Starlight Cinemas to replace several physical servers.
items.answer: Points in favour: better use of hardware; lower power, space and cost; easy backups and migration; isolation between services. Points against / limitations: single physical failure affects many VMs; performance overhead; licensing and expertise costs; resource contention. Conclusion: virtualisation is usually beneficial with redundancy and monitoring in place.
items.markingKey: Up to 4 marks for relevant technical points correctly applied to the scenario; up to 5 marks for developed explanation that weighs both sides and reaches a justified conclusion. Indicative content: better use of hardware; lower power, space and cost; easy backups and migration; isolation between services. / single physical failure affects many VMs; performance overhead; licensing and expertise costs; resource contention.
